Get started with tidypptsdd

Source: vignettes/tidypptsdd.Rmd
tidypptsdd.Rmd

中文

tidypptsdd downloads CSV reports from Nedap pig performance test stations. It can export one report for a range of stations and dates, save one report per station and day, and download the previous day’s reports every day on Windows.

Task Function How
One CSV for a range of stations and dates get_csv() HTTP
One CSV per station and day get_csv_auto() HTTP
Choose a CSV report from the website menu download_csv_auto() Chrome or Edge
Download yesterday’s data every day get_csv_schedule() / download_csv_schedule() Windows Task Scheduler

Start with get_csv() or get_csv_auto() when HTTP provides the report you need. Use Chrome or Edge when the report has to be chosen in the website menu.

Install

tidypptsdd runs on Windows with R 4.1.0 or newer. It depends on the Windows-only taskscheduleR, so this also applies to HTTP downloads. Browser downloads need Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge and wdauto 0.2.0 or newer; Java is not needed.

install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("tony2015116/tidypptsdd")

The package was called pptsdd before version 0.1.8. Function names and arguments are unchanged; replace library(pptsdd) and pptsdd:: with tidypptsdd, and create scheduled tasks again (see below).

Store the account

Run file.edit(path.expand("~/.Renviron")) and add the station address and account. The address is the site’s root URL.

NEDAP_URL=https://your-site.vpu-online.cn
NEDAP_USERNAME=your_username
NEDAP_PASSWORD="your_password"

Restart R, then set up the values used by the examples:

library(tidypptsdd)

url <- Sys.getenv("NEDAP_URL")
username <- Sys.getenv("NEDAP_USERNAME")
password <- Sys.getenv("NEDAP_PASSWORD")
download_path <- file.path(path.expand("~"), "tidypptsdd-data")

stopifnot(all(nzchar(c(url, username, password))))

Replace the station numbers and dates below with ones that have data.

Download over HTTP

One CSV for stations 606 to 608 and 18 to 19 February 2024:

get_csv(
  url = url, username = username, password = password,
  location_min = "606", location_max = "608",
  date_min = "2024-02-18", date_max = "2024-02-19",
  download_path = download_path,
  show_message = TRUE
)

One CSV per station and day, here four reports. Station numbers are strings; dates can be Date values or YYYY-MM-DD strings.

get_csv_auto(
  url = url, username = username, password = password,
  location = c("606", "608"),
  date = seq(as.Date("2024-02-18"), as.Date("2024-02-19"), by = "day"),
  download_path = download_path,
  show_message = TRUE
)

Download through Chrome or Edge

Start the WebDriver service for the browser, then give the position of the CSV report in the website’s report list with csv_position.

driver_dir <- "C:/webdriver"
connect_to_browser(dest_dir = driver_dir)

download_csv_auto(
  url = url, username = username, password = password,
  csv_position = "1",
  location = c("606", "608"),
  date = "2024-02-18",
  download_path = download_path
)

For Edge, add browser = "edge" to both calls. In mainland China, run options(wdauto.mirror = "npmmirror") before connect_to_browser() so the driver is downloaded from a mirror. Stop the service with disconnect_from_browser() (Chrome) or disconnect_from_browser(browser = "edge").

Schedule a daily download

This task runs every day at 20:00, starting tomorrow, and downloads the previous day’s data. Write startdate in the date format of the Windows regional settings; the example uses year/month/day.

task_args <- list(
  url = url,
  username = username,
  password_env = "NEDAP_PASSWORD",
  location = c("606", "608"),
  download_path = download_path
)

get_csv_schedule(
  taskname = "nedap_csv_daily",
  schedule = "DAILY",
  starttime = "20:00",
  startdate = format(Sys.Date() + 1L, "%Y/%m/%d"),
  rscript_args = task_args
)
  • The task reads the password from the environment variable named in password_env when it runs, so set it for the account that runs the task.
  • For browser downloads use download_csv_schedule() with c(task_args, list(csv_position = "1")), and add browser = "edge" for Edge. The WebDriver service must be running.
  • Logs are written to C:/Temp/tidypptsdd/. Delete the task with taskscheduleR::taskscheduler_delete("nedap_csv_daily").

Results and troubleshooting

Reports are filed by station: NonEmptyCSVs/<station>/ for reports with data rows and EmptyCSVs/<station>/ for reports with only a header. File names contain the report date and the download date, for example location606_2024-02-18data_2024-02-20download.csv.

Problem Check
Login fails or the response is not a CSV The root URL, the account and its report permissions. Export the same report by hand in a browser.
Reports land in EmptyCSVs Whether the station has data for that day on the website.
Browser downloads time out The browser, its WebDriver service, and the report at csv_position.
Works by hand, fails as a task Whether the task account can read the password variable and write to the folder; the task log.
